data.name: Marduf
data.gender_notes: Marduf is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Arabic root 'r-d-f', meaning 'to rise, ascend, or exalt'. In Islamic context, it can be interpreted as one who is exalted, raised, or ascended to a high status or rank. The name Marduf carries the meaning “Ascending, Exalted” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Marduf usually hope their child will grow to embody ascending, exalted and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing spiritual growth and ascension towards Allah.
data.etymology: Marduf belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Ascending, Exalted.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Marduf total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

historical_references.context: Marduf ibn Amr al-Ashja'i, a Berber chieftain, rose to power in North Africa (Maghreb) in the late 7th and early 8th century. He was one of the earliest Berber rulers to establish a centralized state and significantly expanded the territories under Berber control.

historical_references.context: Marduf ibn al-Aas ibn al-Harith al-Fihri, who ruled Andalusia (Iberian Peninsula) in the late 8th century, was a powerful Umayyad governor. He is best known for his military campaigns against the Visigoths and for establishing the Umayyad rule in Cordoba.
